_note: Literature in English, Form 1 Teacher's Book. Sibling of the Form 1 Learner's Book in ../Form 1 Learners Books/.
//cover: The manuscript ships NO usable picture of its own. Its four media files are two copies of a 128x128 JPEG of crumpled brown paper, a 231x149 PNG and an empty GIF, and the engine took the 128px paper texture as the cover hero - 33 DPI at the size it is placed, about a ninth of the 300 DPI floor, and a picture of nothing. It cannot be upscaled, because there is no detail in it to reconstruct; house style is that a useless picture is REPLACED, not left and not deleted. For a while the replacement was the firelit storytelling scene its sibling Learner's Book carries, accepted only because this book had nothing else to offer - but using the SAME photograph on both covers of a family is what you avoid if you can, and now there is no need to: cover-src.jpeg is a picture made for THIS book. A teacher reads an open literature anthology with six Form 1 learners around a library table; the blackboard behind them reads Literature - Read, Analyse, Understand, Appreciate, a map of Zambia hangs beside it, and two bound volumes titled Literature and African Literature sit on the table. It satisfies the standing picture rules together: the subject is unmistakably this book's, the learners are Form 1 age, and three of them carry a visible disability - a wheelchair user at the left, an albino learner beside her, and a learner wearing a hearing aid at the right. Of the six learners three are girls and three are boys (the seventh figure is the teacher). Resolution: the source is 1080x809, which is 210 DPI at the 130.8x98mm the literary cover places the hero at, so it was upscaled 4x with Real-ESRGAN to 4320x3236 and resampled down to 2400x1798 - 466 DPI, comfortably over the floor, without carrying a 17MB plate into the PDF. The two covers are still told apart by their field colour: the Teacher's Guide masthead and bottom band are deepened to #3a151e against the Learner's Book's #6b2737. That shift did not used to reach this layout - the engine moved covSignature, which only the landscape syllabus spread reads, while a portrait cover paints its field from covPrimary - and it now moves both, so no coverColor is pinned here.
//synthesiseCover: The manuscript's own title page reads only 'LITERATURE IN ENGLISH TEACHER'S BOOK' and never says Form 1, so the cover the engine lifted from it carried no level tag while the sibling Learner's Book reads 'FORM 1 - LEARNER'S BOOK'. Forcing a synthesised cover builds it from the detected title, subject, book type and level instead, so the two covers carry the same furniture.
//contents: The manuscript hand-types its own table of contents and the engine builds a fresh one from the headings, so every fault below was in the HEADINGS themselves, not in the contents page. UNITE for UNIT is the consequential one: the engine detects a unit by the word, so "UNITE 1" and "UNITE 2" were never recognised as units and their entries sat indented under ACKNOWLEDGEMENTS instead of opening their own level. LITURATURE is a straight misspelling in the same line. UNIT THREE is untitled exactly as it was in the sibling Learner's Book, and is given the same NAME: SUBJECT shape its siblings carry. PRAISES is numbered 1.6.3 where its neighbours run 1.2.1.4 PROVERBS, 1.2.1.5 SONGS and 1.2.1.7 IDIOMS, so it is the missing 1.2.1.6. The RIDDLES heading is typed "Subtopic. 1.2.1.3:" with the full stop where the colon belongs, which the prefix normaliser could not read and which printed as "SUB-TOPIC . 1.2.1.3: RIDDLES". COMPOSING SHORT STORIES is a real sub-topic that simply lost its SUBTOPIC prefix. None of this is engine work - it is one manuscript's typing.

replaceExact.with: 5. Learners to explain the line pattern

//strayHeadings: Two separate faults, both about a line being styled unlike the lines it belongs with. "Lesson Procedure" is the label opening the procedure part of a lesson plan and it recurs all through the book; the writer styled this ONE instance Heading2, so that single occurrence climbed into the contents while every sibling stayed out. It becomes a plain bold head - still visible on the page, no longer a section. The poetry lesson's five numbered teaching steps were styled THREE different ways: steps 1 and 2 as Heading4, which the engine emits as #head (bold italic); steps 3 and 4 left as ordinary body paragraphs; and step 5 as Heading1, which is why it alone appeared in the contents. Demoting step 5 to a paragraph would have fixed the contents and left the run just as uneven, so instead steps 3, 4 and 5 are all raised to the same #head its first two siblings already use, and the five now read alike. Step 5 also lost the space after its number and carried a full stop none of the others has, both corrected in replaceExact above so the heading text matches too.
asHead: 4. Purpose of rhymes in a poem
5. Learners to explain the line pattern
//idioms: Sub-topic 1.2.1.7 IDIOMS was written in TWO halves that had drifted apart, not twice. Every properly formed sub-topic in this book carries the same shape - a prose introduction, GENERAL/SPECIFIC COMPETENCES with the syllabus code, EXPECTED STANDARDS, materials, then the lesson procedure - and RIDDLES and DRAMA both show it whole. Idioms had the first half sitting at the TOP of Unit Two, ahead of 1.2.1.1 FORMS OF ORAL LITERATURE, carrying the introduction and the only occurrence in the whole book of the numbered competence 1.2.1.7.1; and the second half in its correct slot after 1.2.1.6 PRAISES, carrying the lesson procedure but a competence with no number on it at all - the only unnumbered one in the book. Neither half is a duplicate of the other: they share exactly one paragraph of 94 and 43. So the first half is MOVED down to meet the second, which restores both the ascending sub-topic order and the shape every other sub-topic has, and the second half's heading is dropped because the two are now one section under one title. Nothing is deleted but that repeated heading, and the stray "TOPIC: 1.2.1 Oral Literature" line that existed only to introduce the displaced half and duplicated the real topic heading six sections later.
//poetry: Sub-topic 1.2.2.4 POETRY has THREE specific competences, and the book gives each its own section - which is its convention, not a fault. PROSE does the identical thing: sub-topic 1.2.2.2 PROSE carries the first competence, and its second, 1.2.2.2.2 Compose short stories, gets a section headed "1.2.2.2.2 COMPOSING SHORT STORIES". So the manuscript runs two tiers of heading: a sub-topic is written "SUBTOPIC: <code> NAME", and a further competence inside one is written as the bare five-part code plus its name. Poetry's second and third sections simply lost their codes and were typed "SUBTOPIC: POETRY" and "SUBTOPIC: POEMS", which is what made poetry look like three sub-topics under two spellings. They are restored to the PROSE shape: 1.2.2.4.2 PERFORMING POEMS and 1.2.2.4.3 REVIEWING POEMS. The third's competence line was a straight copy of the second's - both read "1.2.2.4.2 Perform Poems", and it is the only SPECIFIC COMPETENCE in the book written in the singular, which is the copy showing - so it becomes 1.2.2.4.3 Review poems. The number follows from the sequence and the verb from the section's own opening sentence, "Reviewing poems involves analysing content and meaning, poetic devices and techniques, structure and organisation". Note for the author: the third competence's wording is inferred from its content, not taken from the syllabus, so it is worth a glance.
